answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor has already been onboarded once (memory_c2), cut unit cost sharply, invoiced accurately, and now quotes a price that meets the 18 % cost-reduction mandate on its own. memory_c6 confirms multi-year commitments can unlock additional volume pricing without narrowing service scope, potentially deepening the margin gain. With finance mandating the cut and the primary contract expiring in 14 days with no auto-renew, switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor satisfies both the cost objective and the timeline. memory_c3 (adding a second source) is noted but deferred to the next cycle because capacity allows only one decision and the assembly line is already at 94 % with no buffer; the immediate risk of a lapsed primary contract outweighs the benefit of a dual-source structure this cycle. Renegotiating with the incumbent would not plausibly hit 18 % without prior multi-year leverage, and deferral risks an uncontracted gap.
